title: HashMap thread safety in practice
context: What goes wrong when HashMap is shared between request threads?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java collections questions (2 of 2)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Requests share the map and write to it without a lock, so entries can vanish, counts can be wrong, and reads can return stale or partly written values. The bug shows up only under load, so it is hard to reproduce. A shared static HashMap used as a cache is a common cause. Fix it with ConcurrentHashMap, with compute and merge for atomic updates, or by keeping the map local to one thread.

points.title: Shared static maps
points.why: A static HashMap used as a cache is written by every request thread without protection.

points.title: Atomic updates
points.why: compute and merge on ConcurrentHashMap update a key atomically.
